seen_animation: A line-drawn lobster seen head-down from the front: the body hangs from the top edge with a horizontal band line, and two V-notched claws hang down on either side above a grey table edge; a small grey lobster sits at far left. In frames 1-3 both claws hang down. From frame 4 the right-hand claw swings inward and up, in frames 5-7 it lies across the lower body with its pincer pointing left, and frames 8-16 hold that pose with the claw crossing in front of the body and the left claw's arm, with only small shifts. The left claw stays hanging throughout.
seen_film: A large real lobster faces the camera on a cloth-covered table, with a smaller lobster at left. In frames 1-2 its right claw (screen right) hangs at the right edge, partly out of frame. In frames 3-4 the claw curls inward and down, in frame 5 it rises and swings left across the lower body, and by frames 6-8 it lies horizontal across the front of the body with the pincer pointing left over the base of the left claw. Frames 9-16 hold this pose with slight claw and antenna adjustments. The left claw hangs still throughout.
named_subject: A lobster (the doodle's oval body with a band line and two V-notched claws, drawn upside down / head-down to match the camera view).
evidence: e.png 1-7 hold both claws down while f.png 1-6 hold the right claw at the frame edge; e.png 8-11 the right claw swings in and down toward the centre as f.png 8-11 curls the claw inward; e.png 12-14 the claw rotates to horizontal and crosses the body as f.png 12-14 lifts it across; e.png 15-17 settle it horizontal across the left claw arm as f.png 15-17 do; e.png 17-50 hold with small shifts as f.png 17-50 do. g.png shows one continuous fan of right-claw positions from lower right to across the body with no reversals. The fastest change is e.png 13 to 14 (claw rotates about 40 degrees and the body's lower outline disappears behind it), which matches the film's fast lift at f.png 13-14 where the claw occludes the body. The left claw, body and scenery stay fixed, as in the film.
primary_gap: The swung claw is smaller and thinner than the film's: in f.png 17-50 the claw spans from the left claw to the right frame edge as a broad mass, while in e.png 17-50 it reaches only from the left claw arm to about the body's right edge and reads as a thin outline.
closes_when: In e.png 15-50 the crossed right claw extends further right and is drawn broader (comparable in width to the hanging left claw), so its size matches the claw in f.png 15-50 without changing the doodle's straight-segment stroke style.
protect: The timing of the swing (start near frame 8, crossing by 14, settle by 17, long hold after), the unchanging left claw, body and scenery, the doodle's straight-segment V-notched claws and band line, and the continuous fan-shaped claw path shown in g.png.
identity_gap: The character is the doodle flipped head-down with the same oval body, band line and V-notched straight-stroke claws; the only departure is that the swung claw in the settled pose is drawn as a thinner, more angular shape than the doodle's claws.
